agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (January 5,
2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be
publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be live
streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to bsaleaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as
states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of California, and a federal
emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would
present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This way the public, the staff, and the Council will
not be physically in the same place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which are not listed on the agenda
but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission and staff
will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members
of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign
up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the public
was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this meeting
because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for
the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an item
may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining
vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded
from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission
first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set
forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the rules
as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing bsaleaumua@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Environmental Sustainability
Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II]. Requests for use of
audio or video equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to Alex Montano at (310) 456-2489, ext. 227, or
amontano@malibucity.org before 12:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 11th day of February 2022 at 1:30 p.m.

  A.  Temporary Skate Park Attendance
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report regarding Temporary Skate Park
  attendance from January to December 2021.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated staff could not provide separate attendance data for residents and non-

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department during January 2022.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in January 2022.

RECREATION

Aquatics: Registration for the Spring quarter of the Malibu Aquatics Foundation
Seawolves Swim Team and Adult Masters Conditioning opened on January 28. Seventy
participants pre-registered for the program which begins February 14.

Community Classes: In partnership with the Boys and Girls Club of Malibu, afterschool
programs began on January 24 and included karate, science, and yoga. A total of seventy
students in grades TK through 5 enrolled in the Malibu Elementary School and Webster
Elementary School programs.

Outdoor Recreation: The January full moon hike at Charmlee Wilderness Park was
canceled due to low enrollment. Staff posted marketing materials, including banners and
posters at Charmlee Park to help increase awareness of the program.

Seniors: Outdoor senior fitness programs continued in January at Malibu Bluffs Park, with
an average of twenty participants per week. New programs added in January included Mat
Yoga and Chair Yoga.

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Skate Programs: Learn to Skate Programs instructed by Champ Camp were added from
January through March following feedback from residents. The January session reached
maximum capacity with fifteen participants, ages 6 to 13.

Social Media: Department social media posts featured lap swim hours, City park
information, afterschool programs, and art exhibits. Hashtags and tagging instructors and
schools on the Instagram story increased views by 30%.

Special Events: Nineteen students from various local schools, including Our Lady of
Malibu School, Malibu Elementary School, and Malibu High School, submitted artwork for
the 2022 Student Art Exhibit. The exhibition will be on display from February 14 through
March 14 at the Art Voyagers Gallery located at Malibu Bluffs Park and online at
Malibucity.org/studentartexhibit.

Over 75 car enthusiasts attended Cars and Coffee at Malibu Bluffs Park on January 9 and
23.

Sports: Winter sports programs began the week of January 23, including Beginning and
Intermediate Youth Tennis and Youth Soccer. Twenty students participated in the weekly
tennis program at Malibu High School, and forty-five students participated in the soccer
program at Malibu Bluffs Park.

The Youth Basketball Program was extended two weeks through February 19 due to
inclement weather in January.

PARK MAINTENANCE

Equestrian Park: Maintenance staff replaced a broken faucet and painted over restroom
graffiti in the men’s restroom.

Las Flores Park: Maintenance staff closed restrooms due to flooding caused by heavy
rain. Maintenance and custodial staff assisted with mud, dirt, and debris clean-up from the
floors and walls before the facility was reopened for public use.

Legacy Park: The Anchor for Malibu bronze placard was removed and reattached with
concrete anchors and stronger adhesive.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Maintenance staff replaced a broken doorknob on the scorekeeper’s
box on the Major Field.

Assembled a new set of bleachers for the Pony Field and anchored the bleachers to the
concrete slab. A car accident, which occurred after hours, destroyed the previous set of
bleachers.

Installed a storage locker within the Temporary Skate Park for chains and locks.
  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Connected a new domestic waterline in the maintenance yard for a quick coupler to supply
clean water for pressure washing and cleaning of hand tools.

Completed turf renovations on the Multipurpose Field and removed the temporary fence
surrounding the area.

Repaired the safety railing guard rails surrounding the skate bowl with new treated wood
and weatherproof deck screws.

Michael Landon Center: Added lockboxes to outlets in the men’s and women’s restrooms.

Trancas Canyon Park: Maintenance staff cleaned and removed all equipment in the
storage area at Trancas Canyon Park. Managed Career Solutions (MCS) staff will
temporarily use the space for tool storage while working at Trancas Field.

Applied 50 yards of mulch to landscape planters.

The dog park display case was removed as a safety precaution due to damage sustained
from high winds.

Subject:  Chumash Day

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review the modified 2022 Chumash Day event and provide
feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION: The City’s Annual Chumash Day event is a Native American Powwow and
Intertribal Gathering coordinated by the Community Services Department. Staff work with
Chumash elders to coordinate the event, which includes traditional dances, songs, arts,
and Native American stories. It is the largest event organized by the City event and typically
takes place over two days during the second weekend in April at Malibu Bluffs Park.
The event regularly draws approximately 3,000-4,000 attendees total for both
days. The City canceled the event in 2020 and 2021 due to COVID-19 and
restrictions on public gatherings.

The event requires a City Temporary Use Permit (TUP), which includes various approvals
by the Sheriff’s Department, Fire Department, County of Los Angeles Department of Public
Health (County), Public Works Department, Environmental and Sustainability Department,
and Planning Department. Due to the number of attendees, staff coordinates additional
restrooms, trash and recycling disposal, onsite security, and various rentals. Public
parking is available at the Ioki property, and the City provides a free shuttle service to-and-
from Malibu Bluffs Park. Onsite parking is reserved for event performers, dignitaries, and
disabled persons.

The 22nd Annual Chumash Day event is scheduled to take place on Saturday, April 9,
2022, from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Staff reviewed County event guidelines and will follow
all requirements to ensure the safety of participants and attendees. All staff and
contractors will be required to wear masks and reminded to wash their hands regularly
and maintain physical distancing whenever possible.

  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item #5.A.
 Additionally, staff modified various aspects of the event plan to further limit potential
COVID-19 concerns, including:
  •  Reducing the event to a one-day event
  •  Limiting arts and craft vendors with distancing between booths
  •  Limiting food vendors to allow food trucks only
  •  Encouraged vendors to accept cashless payments and mobile orders for food
  •  Providing shuttles for single riders and distancing measures in larger vehicles
  •  Providing additional drivers via rideshare services in the Civic Center area
  •  Vaccination requirements for performers
  •  Adding hand-sanitizing and handwashing stations throughout the event
  •  Adding signage related to health and safety measures and precautions
  •  Adding signage with QR codes rather than providing paper hand-outs
  •  Relocating staff break areas to an outdoor location
  •  Hiring custodial staff to ensure regular sanitizing and cleaning of facilities

The Commission is asked to review the 2022 Chumash Day event, and provide feedback
to staff.
